messages.subject: Hypothesis Testing for coefficients
parts:
Dear INLA-experts,

I would like to ask if there is a way in which we can do hypothesis testing for a model's covariates.
Something like: $\log(y)= \beta_1* x_1 + \beta_2* x_2 + \beta_3 * x_3$, and our null hypothesis is: H_0: $\beta_1=\beta_2=\beta3$. 



Thank you in advance

Nancy

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Hypothesis Testing for coefficients
parts:
On Sun, 2015-09-06 at 08:36 -0700, Nancy Jin wrote:
> Dear INLA-experts,
>
> I would like to ask if there is a way in which we can do hypothesis
> testing for a model's covariates.
> Something like: $\log(y)= \beta_1* x_1 + \beta_2* x_2 + \beta_3 *
> x_3$, and our null hypothesis is: H_0: $\beta_1=\beta_2=\beta3$.

with informative priors you can compare the marginal likelihood under
H0 and H1, as H0 just says

\beta * (x1 + x2 + x3)

H
